answer: A staking bond works like a tundra checkpoint: every agent must lock collateral that is slashed if its identity is proven fake. Peers mirror each other's behavior logs and compare them, so a swarm of clones copying one pattern stands out instantly. Creating thousands of bonded identities costs real capital, and a gale of fake accounts cannot pass the bond check without paying for each one — Sybil profit collapses when each fake identity must stake more than it can earn.
